validity.researcher_notes: Existence: confirmed. This is a real, well-documented Gazprom trunk -- energybase.ru carries a dedicated database object (ID eb#pipe00159) with full technical specs, a 2025/2026-dated defect-repair procurement contract names this exact segment ('Leningrad-Vyborg-Gosgranitsa II') and its operating subsidiary (Gazprom Transgaz Saint Petersburg / Severnoye LPU), a 2004 published encyclopedia (Vyakhirev, ISBN 5-85270-327-3) documents its 1973 construction and the 'Severnaya' compressor station, and a DW article (read for context, not cited as a proposed_ref since it does not name this pipeline directly -- it only names the Imatra entry point) corroborates the corridor was actively carrying export gas to Finland until the May 2022 halt. Classification (transmission, gas) is clearly correct given the scale (1220mm/9.13bcm-y/international export). No duplicate-PHYSICAL-pipe concern: I and II are genuinely two separate parallel strings (the 2025/2026 procurement record specifically maintains 'II' as its own asset, distinct from I), consistent with this corridor's known twin-string configuration -- so this is NOT the 'documents describe one pipe' bar for a duplicate flag. CAVEAT (spec, not existence/duplicate): the DATA on this row and on sibling P2335 appear to be copy-pasted from the same undifferentiated energybase source object rather than independently sourced per string -- both rows currently carry an IDENTICAL 115km/1220mm/9.13bcm/y, and GEM's own citation list for this shared wiki page flags an unresolved second length figure (162 km, 1973) that its own internal logic (Start Year attached to I, not II) points toward belonging to I specifically. For THIS row (II), I found row-specific corroboration the 115 km figure is right (the II-named 2025/2026 procurement record's route markers run to 103.3 km, consistent with 115 km once station/valve offsets are included), so I am not contesting II's own Length/Diameter/Capacity -- but I could not similarly corroborate Construction/Start for II (left UNRESOLVED rather than assume the 1973/162km evidence applies here), and the sibling row likely needs its Length corrected. Capacity's '9.13 bcm/y (total for the pipeline)' gloss on GEM's own page is not stated by the underlying source and I found no independent evidence either way on whether it's a per-string or combined figure -- noted, not contested.

The 2025/2026-dated defect-repair procurement contract is the decisive evidence that the physical asset itself remains in active service within the domestic/Gazprom system regardless of the 2022 export halt: Gazprom does not fund pipeline-defect repairs on a line it has abandoned. No source anywhere suggests physical decommissioning, mothballing, or abandonment of this specific string.
